newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's property sale to go ahead - PM.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's property sale to go ahead - PM.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said the government's plans to sell state property would not be hindered by last week's court annulment, which appeared to be a setback to his economic plans.

"The government has the authority to sell them," Erbakan told members of his Welfare Party at a meeting in parliament. "This doesn't change anything. However it comes about, the programme will go ahead."
The constitutional court annulled the property sell-off law, which was announced in September, after 113 deputies from two opposition left-wing parties sought its cancellation.

Erbakan's coalition government hoped to raise 300 trillion lira ($2.9 billion) from the sell-offs which are among a series of measures ultimately aimed at raising over $50 billion in the country's fight against soaring inflation and big deficits.

Since coming to power in late June, Erbakan has focused on privatisation and pushing through measures such as the property sales, leasing power stations and issuing foreign currency debt as ways of restore stability to the country's shaky finances.

Turkey's economy is struggling under the heavy burden of 80 percent annual inflation and a budget deficit expected to widen to 1,300 trillion lira, or 10 percent of gross domestic product, by the end of 1996.
